summary: Eleven comment-endorsed tools, game-development resources, and science reads from a verified full-tree crawl.
telegram_footer: 11 items surfaced | 30/30 prior-day front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: rqlite
items.summary: Distributed SQLite database; warmly recommended by a production control-plane user.
items.why_included: An explicit production endorsement praised both the database and its maintainer.
items.evidence: A production user chose rqlite for an observability control plane and warmly recommends it.

evidence_sources.author: joostdecock
evidence_sources.excerpt: We use rqlite in production, it's the database we chose for (the control plane of) an open source observability solution we're building (morio.it). Just came here to say two things: - rqlite is amazing and warmly recommend

items.name: Dagger
items.source_story_title: Roku developer repositories moved from GitHub to GitLab
items.summary: Container workflow SDK; praised for matching local and CI runs with remote caching.
items.why_included: A hands-on user explained concrete benefits beyond container builds.
items.evidence: A Dagger user praises consistent local and CI workflows, remote caching, and reusable SDKs.

evidence_sources.author: verdverm
evidence_sources.excerpt: Yes, I use Dagger, it's much more than building containers - Container based workflows are the same in CI and locally (you can run containers too), they become one-liners - Remote caching out of the box without extra steps - Multiple language SDKs, unlocks the DAG in BuildKit and containers, real reuse

items.name: GhidraSQL
items.summary: SQL interface to Ghidra; praised for exposing agent tools as virtual tables.
items.why_included: A reverse-engineering experiment produced a specific endorsement of the tool-interface design.
items.evidence: A commenter used GhidraSQL in a reverse-engineering benchmark and argues its virtual-table interface deserves more attention.

evidence_sources.author: nekitamo
evidence_sources.excerpt: I think representing tools for AI as virtual SQL tables is much better than traditional MCP servers, and that this approach deserves a lot more attention. Props to Elias Bachaalany for thinking out of the box and putting it together

items.name: Performance Analysis and Tuning on Modern CPUs
items.source_story_title: How close can pure functional programming get to C?
items.summary: CPU performance book recommended for bridging software patterns and hardware behavior.
items.why_included: A concrete book recommendation emerged from a discussion of memory-access performance.
items.evidence: A commenter names Denis Bakhvalov's book as their best resource for bridging software and hardware.

evidence_sources.author: whilenot-dev
evidence_sources.excerpt: The best one I can come up with is Performance Analysis and Tuning on Modern CPUs

items.name: VDO.ninja
items.summary: Browser-based low-latency video links for phone webcams, remote watch parties, and calls.
items.why_included: An unsolicited first-hand endorsement covered several practical uses beyond OBS.
items.evidence: A user praises its lightweight browser video transport and describes using it for webcams, remote movies, calls, and screen streaming.

evidence_sources.author: NamTaf
evidence_sources.excerpt: Adjacent to OBS, I want to give an unsolicited shoutout to VDO.ninja. It's a very lightweight way to push low latency video between devices via the browser. I've used it to turn my phone into a webcam, to jointly watch movies remotely (with simultaneous voice chat included), to make a multi-person video call, to stream my phone's screen to my desktop, etc All kinds of cool uses.

items.name: func_godot
items.source_story_title: The Quake Fan who built the map editor everybody uses
items.summary: Godot map importer; praised for bringing TrenchBroom levels into playable prototypes.
items.why_included: A first-hand user explicitly praised the import workflow for rapid prototyping.
items.evidence: A user reports successful imports of triggers, lights, materials, and sounds, and calls the workflow awesome for prototyping.

evidence_sources.author: paczki
evidence_sources.excerpt: func_godot works better than I expected it to the first time I used it, properly imports and compiles triggers, lights, materials, sounds, etc straight from trenchbroom so you really can do 90% of your work in trenchbroom. It's awesome for prototyping!

items.name: µCity design documentation
items.source_story_title: How to run a city builder on 16 MHz
items.summary: Game Boy Color city-builder design notes praised for explaining constrained simulation.
items.why_included: The recommendation points to substantive implementation documentation rather than a passing game mention.
items.evidence: A commenter praises the in-depth documentation explaining how a lively city simulation fits an 8-bit machine.

evidence_sources.author: retrac
evidence_sources.excerpt: The author has some great in-depth docs about the design, and how they managed to make a fairly lively-seeming simulation fit into a machine with an 8 MHz 8-bit processor.

items.name: Catlike Coding
items.summary: Graphics-programming tutorials; independently praised as a consistently good learning resource.
items.why_included: A comment independently endorses the tutorial resource rather than merely repeating the story subject.
items.evidence: A commenter praises Catlike Coding as a good resource over a long period.

evidence_sources.author: coinfused
evidence_sources.excerpt: Catlike coding is such a good resource and has been for a long time. Thanks Jasper Flick!

items.name: Oxygen: The Molecule That Made the World
items.source_story_title: Rise of collagen-eating microbes may help explain gaps in the fossil record
items.summary: Nick Lane's science book about oxygen and life; named a reader favorite.
items.why_included: An explicit favorite-book endorsement adds a substantial science read to the tool-heavy intake.
items.evidence: A commenter calls Nick Lane's Oxygen a favorite.

evidence_sources.author: vibrio
evidence_sources.excerpt: Nick Lane’s book “Oxygen“ is a favorite.

items.name: Why Birds Can Fly Over Mount Everest
items.source_story_title: Rise of collagen-eating microbes may help explain gaps in the fossil record
items.summary: Science essay connecting high-altitude birds to deep evolutionary history; praised for lively writing.
items.why_included: A specific, enthusiastic reading recommendation offers an accessible evolutionary rabbit hole.
items.evidence: A commenter loves the essay's first-principles explanation and praises its funny, light writing.

evidence_sources.author: williamdclt
evidence_sources.excerpt: I love this blog article which explains "Why Birds Can Fly Over Mount Everest" from ~first principles starting 450 million years ago, involving the appearance of lignin and the lack of biological processes to break it down. Very funnily and lightly written, just lovely overall:
